name: tutorial-steps-visual
description: Step-by-step visual walkthrough of the Tutorial Pit with per-step screenshots, played honestly (#1517, from #1338): real starting cash, no skill grants or vehicle-driver bootstraps, no forced win. Guided tutorial steps, then free play through fillable sales (#1363: the win counts operating profit, so the console clock ends the level after two sales; the browser's clock burns wages between clicks, so interaction mode plays more, skipped once the level has ended) until the level ends as a genuine victory (levelEndReason completed).

steps.description: Setup: load Tutorial Pit with its real starting cash (#1338: no cash: override -- the tutorial is played on the budget a player actually gets, and every purchase below is a real click).

issue #585: tutorial_start now has a real command-mode implementation too (createRunner.ts), pausing the game the same way the browser boot path (main.ts) always did -- command mode used to report "Unknown command" here and never start anything; now both modes genuinely set state.isPaused = true. The added waitForSelector/waitForTutorialStep only run in interaction mode (command mode has no DOM to wait on) and gate every real click below on the rail actually being armed, mirroring tutorial-interactive.json. #904: the tutorial now opens on hiring (completable immediately, no ticks required) instead of time-speed -- suggesting a faster clock made no sense as the very first card, with an empty site and nothing queued a faster clock would deliver sooner.

Command-mode-only unpause (issue #585): with tutorial_start now genuinely pausing (see its own step above), tickCommand's own loop stops after exactly one real tick while paused regardless of the requested count -- every bare `tick N` below (survey wait, training waits, drill/charge waits, haul wait) would silently advance only 1 tick without this. Interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep-driven steps run their own real clock independent of console pause state, so this resume has no effect there.

hire-surveyor complete: Crew panel opened, Hire clicked, card advances straight to Survey Terrain. tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #923: the speed-control lesson no longer sits here at all -- it moved off this stretch entirely into the box-cut ramp-dig wait further down, so this releases the clock held by tutorial_start's own pause (#585) via advanceToNextStep straight into 'survey'.

Target corrected from the file's original x:15 z:15 to x:23 z:23 (Finding #74 follow-up): the tutorial's survey stage gates its picker to REGION.survey, a single exact point at (23,23) (tutorialStages.ts) -- (15,15) is outside that region and the picker would refuse to confirm it under a real click, the same class Finding #42 already found for un-gated drill grids. Result unaffected: nothing downstream reads survey findings by location, only the flat $3,000 survey cost. tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern.

Issue #716: replaces the four hand-measured `tick 10` blocks (40 ticks total) this step used to be. The seismic survey ordered above actually completes at tick 14 (direct trace: 'Advanced 10 tick(s). Now at tick 10' then '[tick 14] seismic survey complete'), so 26 of those 40 ticks were pure idle padding with nothing left to wait on -- and idle ticks are not free: the surveyor (employee #1) is the same employee who later becomes the box-cut/drill-plan digger (trained driving.excavator further down), and every idle tick between finishing the survey and being handed a real task drains their hunger/fatigue against SitePolicy's own continuous-mode thresholds (60/60, applied at the set-early-policy step below) with nothing to show for it. Direct trace confirmed this padding was the root cause of #716's box-cut deadlock: with it in place, employee #1 starts the walk to board the rock_digger already below both thresholds, SitePolicy's shouldForceRest fires almost immediately (activeActionId gates it while idle, so this only bites once they're finally given real work), interrupts the walk, and each interruption releases the vehicle reservation (interruptActiveAction, GameLoop.ts) -- forcing a full walk back to re-board on top of the rest itself. The cycle compounds (repeated interruptions crash morale to 0 and fatigue to 100 before a single ramp segment is ever dug), so the box-cut stage's own isComplete (a ramp nav-cell count increasing) never fires within the wait's budget. `waitUntil` on `surveyCount` (mirrors `createComparisonStep`'s own `surveyResults.length` check, tutorialSteps.ts) stops the instant the survey actually lands instead of guessing a fixed tick budget -- matching this file's own #689-followup precedent for the drill/charge waits further down.

toggle-survey-overlay complete (#905): clicking the Survey panel's own overlay-toggle button (#496) — panel is already open from the survey step above — clears the confidence quads and the tutorial card advances to hire-driller.

hire-driller complete: Crew panel opened, Hire clicked. tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #553: the tutorial no longer goes straight from here to box-cut -- drilling became queued, vehicle-gated work, so the script now teaches the driving_center, the drill_rig licence and the rig itself first. #681: nor does it go straight to that grind any more -- build-living-quarters and set-early-policy land first, protecting the crew before the long stretch that used to run them into a revolt (#586's own fix shrank the drill grid to dodge this; this closes the actual gap.

#681: build-living-quarters, click half -- the tutorial's new step 3a-i. Placed right after hiring the driller, before the box-cut/drill-plan/charge stretch that runs this crew unmanaged for ~400 ticks: a tier-1 living_quarters gives that stretch's forced rest somewhere real to send a collapsing employee, instead of nowhere at all. #556: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly -- this step only confirms the order landed; the wait step right below drives the site to completion, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own equivalent fix. #1008 follow-up: moved off (18,18), whose footprint included (20,20) -- the exact grid cell a fatigue-interrupted employee near the drill grid can freeze at (clampToGrid, Pathfinding.ts), permanently stranding them once a building occupied it. #1008-followup (PR #1023, CI): (12,15), while flat, deadlocked this exact step in real interaction-mode CI -- its footprint sat only 2-4 tiles from the vehicle spawn point (16,16) and the box-cut corridor (x:16, z:19-31). A first fix attempt moved it to (6,16) (10 tiles clear of those hazards), which traded that deadlock for a different one: a fatigue/rest round-trip livelock -- the walk out to (6,16) and back is long enough that the excavator's fatigue crosses back over the rest threshold before a single box-cut ramp segment carves (confirmed live: `state full`'s navGrid.cellTypeCounts.ramp count never moved across 5000 ticks of direct observation). (29,12) cleared the vehicle spawn, the box-cut corridor, and the drill grid by >=5 tiles each while sitting only 12 tiles (Chebyshev) from the dig site, roughly half (6,16)'s round trip -- see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION.livingQuarters comment for the full trace. #1040: moved again to (29,11), alongside driving_center (29,14) and freight_warehouse (25,12), so the three pins form one stated, checkable compact cluster (TUTORIAL_SITE_CLUSTER_MAX_SPAN_TILES/TUTORIAL_SITE_DIG_ROUND_TRIP_MAX_TILES, balance.ts) instead of each being justified by its own one-off stranding postmortem. #1170 follow-up: the slope-based navmesh (#1151) made a real walking route far longer than the straight-line tile bound the cluster used to be measured against, so the whole cluster moved west of the box-cut corridor to living_quarters (8,15), driving_center (6,15), freight_warehouse (8,18) -- see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION doc comment for the full trace.

#1014: once the living-quarters order lands, the card must show the waiting state -- the stage line swaps to the construction-underway sentence, the WAITING chip becomes visible, and the buy button's highlight is released while it stays clickable (still bs-tutorial-allowed). Screenshot captures the waiting card for the visual channel. Observes only -- the wait_until step right below still owns driving buildingCount to completion. Issue #1014: this step's own timeout (60s) wraps its whole chained interaction array (3x waitForSelector/waitForProperty at 15000ms each, worst case 45s, plus the screenshot) -- the step-level timeout does not budget each action individually (same shape as level2-playthrough-win.json step-96/98), so it is raised well past the 45s worst case rather than split.

interaction.expectedValue: Order placed — waiting for the crew to finish building it.

steps.description: #556/#816: build-living-quarters complete -- the driller or surveyor (both idle, no skill required for place_building) walks to (29,10) and builds the tier-1 living_quarters. First building of the scenario, so buildingCount settles at exactly 1. #1170 follow-up: living_quarters pin moved west of the box-cut corridor to (8,15), alongside driving_center (6,15) and freight_warehouse (8,18) -- see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION doc comment for the full trace.

#681: set-early-policy complete. Selects Continuous under Shift schedule, sets the rest threshold to 65 (rest only restores to 70, so a higher threshold would loop), then Apply. Mirrors tutorial-interactive.json (#1338, #1517).

hire-driver: Crew panel opened, Hire clicked. #556/#1338: the real starting cash covers every purchase up to here, so this step is an ordinary click with no bypass. Opens the Crew panel with ensurePanel rather than a bare toolbar click (#556/#817): with the retired accept step (#1335) moved below build-storage, the step before this one is the manager hire and the panel is already open — the toolbar tab toggles, so a second click would close it, and the rail (which lights the last reachable control) makes that click inert.

#553: buy-drill-rig-assign, first half. Vehicle #1 -- the rock_digger bought below is #2 and the debris_hauler bought further down is #3. #921: a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now (VehicleReservation/ArrivalGate) -- there is no Assign click and no `vehicle driver` command left to issue, so the purchase itself is the whole step and the tutorial rail advances straight to 'train-digger' on the purchase alone; the newly-licensed driller (employee #2) boards the rig on their own once drill-plan below queues vehicle-gated work, with no further player input.

#555: buy-rock-digger-assign, first half. Vehicle #2 -- the drill_rig bought above is #1, and the debris_hauler bought further down is therefore #3. #921: a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now (VehicleReservation/ArrivalGate) -- there is no Assign click and no `vehicle driver` command left to issue, so the purchase itself is the whole step and the tutorial rail advances straight to 'box-cut' on the purchase alone; the newly-licensed digger (employee #1) boards the rock_digger on their own once box-cut's dig_ramp_segment work queues below, with no further player input.

NEW step (Finding #74/#75 follow-up): this file never drove the tutorial's own box-cut stage at all -- the real tutorial requires an access ramp dug before the first shot (tutorialSteps.ts step 4, region-gated to the exact line 16,19-16,31), and with the rail active a real click on the drill grid tool downstream would stay inert until this stage completes. Inserted verbatim from tutorial-interactive.json's own proven box-cut step. buildRampCommand's own depth default is 8 (mining.ts: `named['depth'] ?? '8'`) -- matches this file's own drill_plan depth:8 below with zero stepper clicks needed, unlike the Blast panel's grid tool (default 6). tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the hardcoded `cash: 140364` -- a real CI run produced 138646 (a $1,718 gap), the cumulative real-time payroll/fuel accrual class documented elsewhere in this PR, compounded here by the several player-facing waits between game start and this step (driving-center build, licence training, rig purchase, rig assignment). `decreased` proves the ramp build (and everything before it) spent cash without pinning a host-timing-sensitive cumulative figure. #923 had advanced the card to 'speed-up-for-dig' next; #1015 removes that step (and its 'speed-normal-after-dig' pair) entirely -- the speed bar is unconditionally player-controlled from the tutorial's first step onward -- so box-cut now advances straight to 'drill-plan', same as before #923.

expect.note: ramp build cost $1,200 (buildRampCommand, mining.ts), verified live

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:4 depth:8 start:22,20 diameter:0.089
steps.description: #949-followup: added the spacing (3->4, one increment click, 1m/step) and depth (6->8, two increment clicks, 1m/step) stepper clicks before the drag -- both steppers live on the shared ParamStrip (#bs-param-strip-bar, ParamStrip.ts), rendered the instant the grid tool arms, and were unreachable in this step before tutorialStages.ts's own 'drill-plan' stage allowlisted them (defect 2 fix). Without these clicks the drag alone produced a mis-spaced grid at the panel's own defaults (wrong spacing/depth), not the retuned 3x3/spacing:4/depth:8 plan #949 asks for. #553: confirming the 3x3/9-hole grid now only ORDERS the 9 holes -- drill_hole became queued, vehicle-gated work, so they are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, and the tutorial does not advance to `charge` until they have landed. The wait is the step below; the mid-pattern screenshot above is the ghosts-and-real-holes picture #553 asks for. #949: spacing/depth/start retuned from 3/6/(20,20) to 4/8/(22,20), mirroring the exact retune tutorialSteps.ts's own 'drill-plan' stage applies (verified live against the real engine to rate the shot PERFECT with zero casualties/destruction, replacing the old 5m-spacing/8m-depth-at-(20,20) plan that rated CATASTROPHIC). rows/cols/diameter unchanged (still 3/3/0.089). `dragTiles` moved to (22,20)-(30,28) to match the new footprint. GAP CLOSED: REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts) used to exact-gate the picker to the OLD (20,20)-(26,26) box (#601-followup, this same file's prior note), which would have rejected every tile outside that stale gate for a real click-mode drag (`.claude/rules/scenario-defs.md`: "pickers reject tiles outside the step's region"); the tutorial rail's own region has since been widened/moved to (22,20)-(30,28) alongside this retune, so the drag above lands cleanly. CI cash mismatch fix (unchanged from the prior pass, still applies): this command carries `diameter:0.089`, the real Drill panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M (Drill.ts) -- an omitted diameter falls back to the console-only 0.15 default and computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) scales hole duration by diameter, so this keeps command mode's drill_rig busy-time matching a real click's. Downstream cash/tick checkpoints through the blast step below were re-derived against the new 4/8/(22,20) plan and verified: command-mode run (`npx tsx scripts/run-all-scenarios.ts tutorial-playthrough tutorial-steps-visual tutorial-interactive`) passes with 0 failures, and interaction-mode run (real Puppeteer clicks, screenshots) passes end-to-end confirming Spacing 4.0m/Depth 8.0m/3x3=9 holes and Amount 4kg/Stemming 2.4m reached by real clicks. #1330: superseded by the panel-default retune -- the panel's own defaults are now exactly this plan (grid spacing 4 m, depth 8 m; charge amount 4 kg, stemming 2.5 m), so this step carries no spacing/depth/amount/stemming setStepper actions and any stepper-click wording above is historical.

#689-followup: 1/8 of the drill wait, converted from a fixed `tick 50` chunk to a `waitUntil` on holeCount itself. The fixed 8x50=400-tick budget (see this file's own prior #681 note, preserved below on the final chunk) ran to completion regardless of how long drilling actually took -- direct trace against this file's current command sequence (build_ramp/drill_plan exactly as declared, with the current build-living-quarters at 18,14) shows all 9 holes land by tick 216, ~184 ticks earlier than the fixed budget's tick ~400 landing. Those extra ticks were not idle-and-harmless: two employees with nothing to do still drain hunger/fatigue/morale every tick (needsMoraleEffect, EmployeeNeeds.ts), and running ~300 more ticks than necessary before charging even starts was enough on its own to crash wellBeing to 0 and trigger a real worker_revolt at tick 715 -- reproduced identically regardless of living_quarters position (13,4 or 18,14), so the fixed-tick padding itself, not commute distance, was the remaining cause. Stopping the instant holeCount reaches its target removes the wasted ticks; direct trace of the resulting shorter trajectory reaches the charge/blast stretch below with wellBeing comfortably positive and no revolt.

expect.note: #555 regression guard: the box-cut+drill-plan stretch above is ~250+ ticks of two employees' continuous vehicle-gated work with no living_quarters anywhere in this file's own script -- exactly the pacing that drove wellBeing to a permanent 0 and a worker_revolt game-over here before this fix (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay had a dead zone at exactly 0: nothing but a strictly positive per-tick delta could ever move a score pinned at the clamped floor, and LevelDef.scoreDecayRate was declared per-level -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- but never actually reached updateScores, which always ran the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Asserting levelEndReason stays null right here, before charge/blast ever run, is what keeps a future pacing stretch from hiding a revolt behind this file's own closing `campaign complete` debug override again. #681 follow-up: `LevelDef.revoltImmune` (which used to make tutorial_pit immune to worker_revolt outright) is gone -- this block now has to survive the real rules, which is why it is split into eight `tick 50` steps instead of one `tick 400` (see 1/8 above).

steps.description: #949: retuned from amount:5 stemming:2 to amount:4 stemming:2.5, mirroring tutorialSteps.ts's own 'charge' stage retune. The click flow now reaches for the amount/stemming steppers explicitly (one decrement click, 5kg->4kg; the amount stepper's step is 1kg, Charge.ts) rather than relying on Charge All at the panel's own 5kg/2m defaults, which is what this step's click sequence used to do when the declared command matched those defaults exactly -- it no longer does. Stemming lands at 2.4m (two increment clicks, 2.0->2.2->2.4; the stemming stepper's own step is 0.2m, Charge.ts) rather than the command's exact 2.5m: the stepper has no way to land on an odd multiple of 0.2 from a 2.0m start, and 2.4m is functionally identical to 2.5m here anyway -- both sit at or above BlastCalc's own full-stemming-effectiveness cap of 0.3x depth (0.3*8=2.4m at this pattern's new depth:8), the same cap this file's own prior note on the buildingCount step below already documents for the old 6m-deep pattern. Command mode fires the plan at the literal 2.5m the tutorial hint declares; interaction mode fires it at the stepper-reachable 2.4m; both are capped-equivalent so the two channels' blast outcomes should not diverge on this account. tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #926: the click only queues the order -- charging is real, per-hole, queued work, so the tutorial stays on 'charge' (and the panel stays on its Charge tab) until every hole has actually landed; the wait step right after is what drains it and is where the tutorial step advance is now asserted, not here (a plain 'value increased' comparison used to complete this step, and the assertion here, on the very first hole -- see that step's own note). The stepper click count/selectors above were verified against a real interaction-mode run (Puppeteer, screenshots), confirming Amount 4kg/Stemming 2.4m reached by real clicks. #1330: superseded by the panel-default retune -- the panel's own defaults are now exactly this plan (grid spacing 4 m, depth 8 m; charge amount 4 kg, stemming 2.5 m), so this step carries no spacing/depth/amount/stemming setStepper actions and any stepper-click wording above is historical.

#689-followup: converted from a fixed `tick 225` block to `waitUntil` on chargedCount itself, same reasoning as the drill-wait chunks above -- direct trace shows all 9 holes charge by tick 363 (147 ticks from when charging starts), ~78 ticks short of the fixed 225-tick budget this step used to always spend regardless. Combined with the drill-wait fix above, the full drill+charge stretch now finishes at tick 363 instead of 715, comfortably clear of worker_revolt's own wellBeing-driven countdown. #926: the tutorial step only advances to 'sequence' once every hole is genuinely charged (tutorialSteps.ts's 'charge' step no longer completes on the first hole alone), which is also exactly when the panel's own auto-advance (BlastWorkshop.ts's suggestStep) moves the Blast Workshop to its Sequence tab -- so the tutorialStep assertion belongs here, at the drain's own completion, not on the charge-all click above.

#707: converges the blast step's own deathCount across command and interaction mode, using the same absolute-tickCount waitUntil idiom as the the retired accept step (#1335) step further down this file (both retargeted together -- see that step's own note for the offer-pool side of this change). forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy (GameLoop.ts) now gives idle employees the same proactive rest as working ones, so once Kurt Pickaxe (driller) and Walt Dusty (surveyor) finish their last queued task they get routed away from the grid toward living_quarters within a handful of ticks -- a tick-by-tick command-mode probe from the chargedCount:9 landing point (npx tsx scripts/scenario-test.ts, custom script replaying this file's own command sequence, then ticking one at a time and firing a throwaway `blast` at each point) found BOTH employees still standing in the blast footprint (Walt mid-dig in the build_ramp start:16,19 end:16,31 shaft, Kurt at the drill grid's own spawn point) for the first 5 ticks after chargedCount lands (deathCount:2), Walt alone for exactly 1 more tick (deathCount:1), and both clear (deathCount:0) from 6 ticks onward, continuously through at least 900 ticks past that point. Command mode's own chargedCount:9 lands at tick 337-338; interaction mode's lands at tick 428 (direct-traced both ways, real interaction-mode run) -- a raw `tick 50` command here does NOT work in interaction mode: tutorial_start's own pause (tutorialRails.ts's clock-hold) means a single multi-tick console command's internal loop breaks after its first iteration once state.isPaused is true (events.ts's tickCommand checks `if (state.isPaused) break` at the end of each loop iteration), so it silently advances only 1 tick regardless of the requested count -- the same class of bug the file's own step-2 "time resume" step already documents as command-mode-only. `waitUntil` sidesteps this entirely (interaction-executor.ts loops the console's own `tick 1` directly, same mechanism `wait_until field:chargedCount`/`field:holeCount` above already rely on, never affected by the pause-triggered early break since each individual `tick 1` call completes its one iteration before any break check matters) -- so this step targets a fixed absolute tickCount (480) comfortably past both modes' own chargedCount-landing tick plus the 6-tick danger window, the same absolute-target technique the file's own the retired accept step (#1335) step below already established (tickCount is reseeded fresh per tick via `new Random(state.seed + state.tickCount)`, so which tick a run's own path happens to land the wait on does not change what a shared target tick means). Verified in both command mode and a real interaction-mode run: deathCount is 0 at the blast step below in both. RETARGETED for #556: the absolute target (tickCount 480) is long behind us — ordering the living quarters and the driving centre is real queued work now, and this beat lands past tick 500. The waitUntil therefore spent its whole 200-tick budget going nowhere, and with wellBeing already at zero coming out of the charge phase those 200 idle ticks ran the revolt clock (REVOLT_TICKS 120) out and ended the level in a worker_revolt before the blast below. What the step is actually for is the handful of ticks it takes forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy to route the crew off the grid, so it is a plain short tick block now rather than an absolute tick target that has to be re-measured every time anything upstream moves. Lengthened 40 -> 60 (#556): the surveyor now shares the charge dispatches, so there are two people to route off the pattern before the shot rather than one.
#1362: FIRE then DETONATE once. DETONATE sounds the horn itself and fires automatically as soon as nobody is left in the danger zone -- no separate Sound the Horn, wait, FIRE sequence.
#1362: wait for the automatic fire -- the blast clears the plan (holeCount 0) only once the evacuation finished and the sequence fired.

Fix (CI regression, two parts). (1) This file's own top-level `skipBlastPlayback` was missing (unlike tutorial-interactive.json, which drills the identical 3x3/9-hole/994-fragment pattern and has carried it since #557) -- added at the file's own top level, since per GameRenderer's own __skipBlastPlayback bridge comment (main.ts) skipping the animation "changes nothing" for a scenario capturing shots of the settled muck pile (this file's own post-step `shots` orbits), and leaving it on costs real wall-clock time downstream of this step (#475) for no visual-regression value this file actually checks. It does NOT by itself rescue this step's own trailing waitForTutorialStep though -- the runner only calls __skipBlastPlayback() AFTER this step's whole interaction array (scenario-interaction-runner.ts's own `cmdSlug === 'blast'` block runs post-step), so it cannot un-block a wait still in flight inside this same step. (2) The actual fix for the wait itself: timeout 40->120 (outer), the trailing waitForTutorialStep's own inner timeout 60000->90000, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own proven 90s/60000ms budget for the byte-identical 9-hole/994-fragment/`isBlastReportOutstanding` (`[data-blast-report-modal]`, tutorialStepHelpers.ts) post-blast advance (tutorialSteps.ts's 'blast' stage, #545/#707) -- direct-traced (isolated interaction-mode repro of this exact workload, multiple runs) reaching 'scores'/'event-fire-resolve' cleanly well within that budget every time, while two independent FULL 64-step runs against the old 65000ms effective budget both stalled reporting only 1 real tick processed in that window; CI's own real-world timing (more concurrent load than an isolated repro) is exactly the kind of margin a real-time-delay-gated UI transition (BLAST_REPORT_DELAY_MS, #545) can lose across. blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, Blast Report closed. deathCount raised 1 -> 2 (#558 full-disc survey claim follow-up, issue #558/PR #569): step 4's `survey seismic x:23 z:23` claims its full SURVEY_COVERAGE_RADIUS=20 disc (siteExpansion.ts's cellsInDisc), growing the site from the starting 32x32 to 48x48 before the driller is hired at step 7. Employee hire's spawn point is `minX + sizeX/2, minZ + sizeZ/2` -- on this run minX/minZ stay 0 throughout (the site only grows eastward/southward from (0,0), never crosses into negative territory), so that formula numerically equals the pre-#571 `sizeX/2` here; this scenario's deathCount reproduces identically whether or not the #571 origin-offset fix is applied and is NOT evidence for that fix (verified live, both ways). The real driver is #558's site growth alone: on the grown 48x48 site the spawn point resolves to (26, 24), which lands on the real 3x3/spacing-3 drill grid's own footprint (x:20-26, z:20-26) -- x=26 sits exactly on the grid's east edge, z=24 well inside it. (The prior write-up here cited a furthest-throw distance for a drill grid size that was never real -- see the drill_plan step's own #601-followup note -- so that figure is dropped rather than restated unverified for the real grid.) cash is unaffected either way (lawsuits/fines from a death do not deduct immediately). The #571 origin-offset regression itself is covered separately by the unit/integration tests added in 75a06cf, which force a negative origin (x:-4, z:-4). CI cash mismatch fix: cash corrected 70320 -> 70648 (+$328) now that the drill_plan step above carries `diameter:0.089` -- command mode's own drill_rig spent less time (and fuelCostPerTick) sinking all 9 holes once its duration matches what a real click always produced, so more cash survives to this checkpoint. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): that +$328 offset was correct relative to command mode, but the box-cut step several steps up this same file also turned out to carry a real-time-accrual error that compounds forward -- dropped the exact cash figure here too rather than chase a second moving target. Not replaced with `decreased`: as the note above already says, cash is unaffected by this step in either mode (command mode's own trace shows it completely unchanged), so there is no single mode-agnostic cash claim to make -- holeCount/chargedCount/deathCount remain exact since they are not host-timing-sensitive. #555 tutorial worker-revolt fix: a real fix, not a route-around -- the preceding box-cut/drill-plan stretch used to crash wellBeing to a permanently-pinned 0 and flip `state.levelEndReason` to `worker_revolt` before this step ever ran (ScoreManager.ts's `applyDecay` had a dead zone at exactly 0, and `LevelDef.scoreDecayRate` -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- had never actually reached `updateScores`, which always used the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Both are fixed now: `state.levelEndReason` stays null through this step and for the rest of the run, `BlastReportModal` opens and renders normally post-blast (its `state.levelEndReason !== null` guard never trips), and this step is back to a real click sequence identical to tutorial-interactive.json's own proven blast step -- `report-close` is genuinely reachable again, not a permanent dead end. #707 (converged): `forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy` (GameLoop.ts) now gives idle employees the same proactive rest as working ones, and that changed BOTH employees' fates here, not just the surveyor's -- a command-mode probe stepping tick-by-tick from the chargedCount:9 landing point (replaying this file's own command sequence, then ticking one at a time and firing a throwaway `blast` at each point) found deathCount:2 (Walt Dusty AND Kurt Pickaxe both still in the blast footprint) for the first 5 ticks after chargedCount lands, deathCount:1 (Walt alone) for exactly 1 more tick, and deathCount:0 (both clear -- proactively routed toward living_quarters once idle) from 6 ticks past chargedCount:9 onward, continuously, through at least 900 ticks past that point (the full range tested). No nonzero deathCount is a safe target any more: the earlier #689-followup value (1) was only ever true for a single-tick window in command mode's own timeline, and interaction mode's real per-step polling overhead (`.claude/rules/scenario-defs.md`'s tick-count-divergence class, compounded across this file's 85 steps) can land its own blast tick anywhere relative to that window -- there is no reason to expect it to hit the same single tick command mode does. The new `tick 50` step immediately above (between the chargedCount wait and `event choose 0`) spends 50 idle ticks -- comfortably inside the 6-900 safe window and identical in both modes, since a plain `tick N` with no waitUntil target advances both trajectories by the same fixed amount regardless of where each mode's own overhead already left them -- so this step's own deathCount is 0, verified in both command mode (`npx tsx scripts/scenario-test.ts --scenario tutorial-steps-visual`) and interaction mode (`npm run scenario -- --scenario tutorial-steps-visual --mode interaction`). (#1362: the blast already fired by itself; this step closes its report.)

#1339: build-driving-center, click half -- ordered after the first blast, which leaves oversized boulders only a rock fragmenter can break; the Driving Center teaches its licence. Every role arrives able to do its own job, so the old drill-rig and excavator courses are gone.
#556/#816: build-driving-center complete -- the site finishes construction before the fragmenter course is booked.
#1339: train-fragmenter, click half -- the hired Driver (found by role in the crew panel) is booked on the Rock Fragmenter licence at the driving_center.

#1339: train-fragmenter complete -- the course finishes and the driver holds driving.rock_fragmenter. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick.

#1334: scores card does not auto-dismiss. The player inspects the scores HUD with a real click on #bs-hud-scores (pointerenter/click raise its inspectCount); only that action completes the card, after which the scripted consultant event fires. Waits on the tutorial reaching the next card, not on a delay.

#555 tutorial worker-revolt fix (this PR): restored to a real dialog interaction, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own event-choose step -- the `worker_revolt` game-over this used to route around (UIManager.update() defers EventModal while `state.levelEndReason !== null`) no longer fires (see the blast step's own note), so the scripted `tutorial_synergy_consultant` event dialog is genuinely reachable and answerable again, not a permanent dead end.

The file's original decreased:["safety"] assertion does not survive across both modes (Finding #74/#75 follow-up, discovered live) -- not because the point is wrong, but because it is no longer independently checkable here. In command mode safety still drops exactly on this scripted tick (50 -> 45.05, matching the file's original point precisely). In interaction mode the blast step's own waitForTutorialStep (stepId: ["scores","event-fire-resolve","hire-manager"]) drives the real clock through several ticks while polling for the rail to reach hire-manager -- including the event-fire-resolve stage's own autoCommands: ["tick 3", ...] -- so the safety damage already lands during that wait, before this step ever runs, and by here it reads 35.15 with nothing left to decrease on this specific tick. Same class as the contract-deliver step below: real per-click waiting does not reproduce command mode's precise scripted tick count. cash is unaffected by either mode's path and stays checkable. CI cash mismatch fix: cash corrected 70312 -> 70640 (+$328), the same fixed offset as the blast step above -- this tick spends $8 regardless (70648-8=70640), and the diameter fix's saving carries through unchanged since nothing between the two steps touches cash beyond that single tick's own upkeep. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped the exact figure -- same box-cut-originated real-time-accrual error as the blast step above, which this checkpoint inherits unchanged. Also moved below the event-choose step above (was above it) -- see that step's own note for why: the event is already fired and pending by here, and a plain `tick 1` refuses outright while one is pending (events.ts's tickCommand), so it must run after the dialog is actually resolved, matching what a real player experiences.

hire-manager complete: Crew panel opened, Hire clicked now that the event is resolved. cash not pinned exactly (Finding #74/#75 follow-up, discovered live): the blast step's own multi-target waitForTutorialStep (scores/event-fire-resolve/hire-manager) drives the real clock through several real-time-dependent ticks, draining more wage/upkeep cash than command mode's precise scripted tick count -- a real, verified cross-mode divergence (same class as the tick-1 step above), not a fixed offset safe to hardcode. tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- living_quarters/driving_center/freight_warehouse all complete for real now that place_building's root-cause dispatch livelock is fixed (tickTaskCompletion.ts relocates a bystander stranded on a just-completed building's footprint; EmployeeDispatchSteps.ts lets an idle employee fall through to the open pool instead of freezing behind one permanently-unreachable queued entry), so this step succeeds genuinely. Card sequence follows tutorialSteps.ts’s reordered canonical order (#556/#817): the retired accept step (#1335) now sits after build-storage, so a contract’s deadline no longer starts while a construction site is still going up.

#689-followup: same fragility as tutorial-interactive.json's own the retired accept step (#1335) step (see its note) -- the drill/charge waitUntil fixes above shortened this file's own trajectory enough to shift where it lands relative to the contract offer pool's refresh cycle (REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks, Contract.ts). Direct trace confirms this step now lands at tick 364 with 8 ore_sale offers and no rubble_disposal -- the one type this file can actually deliver later (consumeStoredOre() draws on raw storedMassKg, which the debris hauler fills; ore_sale/supply need specific ore this hauler never produces). The pool's next rubble_disposal offer surfaces after 36 more ticks (tickCount 400), no event pending anywhere in that window, so this waits on tickCount itself (deterministic given the fixed seed) rather than the offer directly -- there is no state-dump field for 'a rubble_disposal offer exists' to wait on instead. Issue #716 follow-up: the survey-wait fix earlier in this file (the `wait_until field:surveyCount` step, replacing four hand-measured `tick 10` blocks) shortened the box-cut/drill-plan employee's pre-work idle time and, with it, this step's own landing tick -- direct trace now lands at tick 338, not 364. The target itself is untouched (`tickCount` is reseeded fresh per tick, `new Random(state.seed + state.tickCount)`, so which contracts the pool holds at absolute tick 400 does not depend on the path taken to get there), but reaching 400 from 338 takes 62 ticks, 2 more than the old 60-tick budget ever needed to cover -- `maxTicks`/`timeoutMs`/the step's own outer `timeout` are widened with margin, matching this file's own convention elsewhere of budgeting past what a direct trace measures rather than pinning the exact figure. #707 follow-up: retargeted again, 400 -> 550 -- this file's own tick 480 landing point (the new waitUntil step above, added to converge the blast step's deathCount across modes) already carries both modes' tickCount past 400 before this step ever starts (command mode reaches this step around tick 480-488, interaction mode around tick 480-500 -- both already past the old 400 target, which a `waitUntil` can never reach once tickCount has already passed it, since tickCount only increases). This step was never actually exercised end-to-end in interaction mode before now -- every prior interaction-mode run failed earlier, at the blast step's own deathCount mismatch, so this staleness went undetected. A direct probe (fresh `campaign start`/`time resume`, ticking forward from 0 and calling `contract list` at each candidate tick, exploiting the same tick-only-determinism the note above already established) found `rubble_disposal` offers continuously present in the pool from roughly tick 400 through at least tick 700 -- not the narrow single-boundary window the original 400 target needed, so any target comfortably past both modes' new, later entry point works. 550 sits with wide margin above both (leaves ~60-150 ticks depending on mode), `maxTicks`/`timeoutMs`/`timeout` widened to match. RETARGETED for #556: the absolute target (tickCount 550) is long behind us for the same reason as the blast-step pad above. What this step buys is one turn of the contract offer pool (REFRESH_INTERVAL 20 ticks, Contract.ts) so a rubble_disposal offer — the one type this file can actually deliver against — is on the board when the accept below runs; a plain 20-tick block buys exactly that without pinning an absolute tick that moves whenever anything upstream does. It also keeps 250 idle ticks of salary off a balance that would otherwise be negative before the warehouse below is ordered.

vehicle-buy-assign, first half: Vehicles panel open, tier-1 hauler bought and placed on the terrain surface. #556/#1338: the real starting cash covers every purchase up to here, so this step is an ordinary click with no bypass. #921: a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now (VehicleReservation/ArrivalGate) -- there is no Assign click and no `vehicle driver` command left to issue, so the purchase itself is the whole step and the tutorial rail advances straight to 'build-storage' on the purchase alone; the driver hired and licensed above (employee #4) boards the hauler on their own once haul-debris queues vehicle-gated work further down, with no further player input.

expect.note: Step-local: the drill_rig and rock_digger bought earlier survive the blast above (evacuateZone genuinely evacuates them clear of it, #557), so the standing fleet count here is 3, not 1 -- not the number of vehicles this file has bought MINUS what the blast destroyed, since nothing did. What this step owns is that the purchase itself lands — one more vehicle, $25,000 gone. cash is asserted directionally, not to the exact figure: interaction mode accrues real-time payroll between the clicks of a step, so an exact changedBy drifts by a few dollars against command mode (this file’s own #553/#586 history documents the same class).

The tutorial's build-storage stage gates its picker to REGION.warehouse, the exact tile (8,18) (tutorialStages.ts) -- #1170 follow-up: moved west of the box-cut corridor, alongside living_quarters (8,15) and driving_center (6,15), see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION doc comment for the full trace. tutorial_start (step 1) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #556/#816: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly -- structurally this step is a genuine success (ordering is valid work under #556), but #556/#1338: the real starting cash covers every purchase up to here, so this step is an ordinary click with no bypass.

steps.description: #556/#816: build-storage complete -- the freight_warehouse site finishes construction, the last of the tutorial's three enforced pins (living_quarters, driving_center, freight_warehouse -- #1040's compact cluster). Screenshot captures the finished layout for visual inspection of the pins' mutual proximity. (root-cause livelock in place_building's dispatch/interruption logic fixed: an idle bystander employee standing on a just-completed building's footprint is now relocated the same way the builder already was, and an idle employee whose own taskQueue holds one permanently-unreachable entry now falls through to the open pool instead of freezing forever). #689-followup: buildingCount was 3 once this landed -- the #681 mitigation earlier in this file (build-living-quarters/set-early-policy steps) also builds a driving_center (step 12, `build driving_center at:6,15`) so the driller can train and crew a drill_rig; that building was never demolished pre-#557, so by this point (living_quarters + driving_center + this freight_warehouse) 3 buildings genuinely stood, not 2. #557: buildingCount was 2, not 3 -- Damage.ts's processProjections attenuates debris out to the full 15m BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M (was an exact 2m HIT_RADIUS only, the audited gap #557 closed), and the OLD 3x3 grid at (20,20)/5kg/2m destroyed the living_quarters at (18,14) -- 6.3m from the nearest hole, well outside the old exact-hit radius but squarely inside the wider one (direct-traced: two hits, 3412 J then a lethal 4380 J, against 120 HP). At that point retuning was attempted and rejected: stemming was already at 2m against the 6m-deep pattern's own 1.8m (holeDepth*0.3) effectiveness cap, so raising it further did nothing (BlastCalc.ts), and the integer-only amount stepper's one available downward step (5kg->4kg) survived the building but downgraded the rating to BAD -- losing the CATASTROPHIC blast that beat existed to demonstrate. #949 changes the premise: the tutorial's own scripted blast is no longer supposed to be catastrophic at all -- a tutorial exists to teach a competent shot, not a disaster -- so the whole pattern retunes together (3x3/spacing:4/depth:8 at (22,20), amount:4kg, stemming effectively 2.4-2.5m, see the drill-plan/charge steps above), verified live for tutorialSteps.ts's own version of this exact plan to rate PERFECT with zero casualties or destroyed buildings. buildingCount is 3 again here, not 2: the living_quarters at (18,14) -- 6.3m from grid center as before, but now well clear of the new grid's own footprint (x:22-30, z:20-28 vs the old 20-26/20-26) as well as blast-energetic enough to survive regardless -- is no longer destroyed. driving_center and the freight_warehouse this step itself just finished both continue to survive as before. buildingCount:3 here is the target outcome verified for tutorialSteps.ts's own plan against the real engine, and this file's own identical geometry (3x3/spacing:4/depth:8 at (22,20)) was independently confirmed via command-mode (`run-all-scenarios.ts`) and interaction-mode (Puppeteer, screenshots) runs, both passing. #1335: the contract accept card was removed from the tutorial (29 steps); haul-debris now follows build-storage directly, so this step lands on haul-debris and no rubble_disposal contract is accepted here -- sell-ore accepts the one fillable ore offer instead.

haul-debris complete (#552): automatic dispatch sends the hauler to a reachable fragment with no player click at all -- the retired Haul button is gone, so there is nothing left for this step to point at. The step teaches watching, not clicking: waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the haul exactly as before, just without a click triggering it. #653 follow-up: command mode's own `command` was widened from `tick 1` to `tick 20` -- verified live (command mode) that storedMassKg is still 0 at tick 10, first lands the hauler's full 1050kg load between tick 11 and tick 13 (walk-to-vehicle/board, drive-to-fragment, load, drive-back, unload all cost real simulated ticks that only started counting once this step's own ticks ran), and stays there afterward; tick 20 keeps ~7-9 ticks of margin over that observed landing point without approaching the accepted contract's 67-tick deadline. issue #585 (merge): the accept step above changed independently on both sides of the merge (scoped click instead of unscoped), shifting exactly when the hauler's dispatch clock starts counting relative to before #653's own 10/13/20-tick measurement; kept at 40 (this branch's own pre-merge value) rather than adopting #653's 20 outright, since a full command-mode replay of the merged file (all 43 steps) is a cheaper, equally valid check than re-deriving the exact new landing tick by hand -- confirmed clean end to end with 40, not re-verified at 20. #707: back down to 20 -- granting employee #1 blasting (a since-removed bootstrap step before drill_plan; #1517 plays honestly) shortens the charging phase enough that the wait_until step above now accepts the rubble_disposal contract at tick 300 instead of 400, and that specific pool instance's own deadlineTicks is 37, not the ~67 #653 measured against a different offer -- `tick 40` alone would cross tick 337 and expire the contract before delivery (direct trace, command mode); `tick 20` lands well inside the deadline while keeping #653's own measured hauler-load margin (loaded by tick 11-13 after dispatch). #928: 20 -> 40 -- direct-traced (command mode) against the current engine: the single-gauge fatigue rebalance shifts this contract's own accept tick earlier (595, down from #707's 300-vs-400 range's own later baseline) and the hauler's driver (employee #4) picks up a detour of real open-pool work (freight_warehouse construction) before ever walking to board the vehicle, pushing storedMassKg's own first nonzero landing to tick 628 (33 ticks after this step's own start at tick 595) -- `tick 20` alone (landing at tick 615) is 13 ticks short. `tick 40` (landing at tick 635) keeps 7 ticks of margin past the 628 landing point while staying inside the accepted contract's own 46-tick deadline (expires tick 641) -- the same margin philosophy #653's own original measurement used, re-measured against today's timing rather than widened blindly. #974 follow-up: 40 -> 44 -- direct-traced (command mode) against the abort-vs-fatigue fix (releaseVehicleReservation now genuinely aborts an in-flight haul instead of the driver silently finishing it underneath a stale reservation): the driver's own single mid-approach forced-rest interruption (before pickup -- isMidLoadedHaul, FragmentTaskLifecycle.ts, protects only the post-pickup to_depot leg from a second one) pushes storedMassKg's first nonzero landing to tick 620 (42 ticks after this step's own start at tick 578) -- `tick 40` alone is 2 ticks short. `tick 44` keeps a couple of ticks of margin past the 620 landing point while staying inside the accepted contract's own deadline (direct-traced: `tick 48` already reports the contract expired/not found, so the safe window here is narrower than #928's own 7-tick margin). #959: the card this step waits for is 'sell-ore', renamed from 'contract-deliver' — the tutorial's own missing beat is now selling the blasted ore for money, not just delivering whatever contract happened to be accepted. #1015 follow-up: 44 -> 22 -- removing the two speed-control steps upstream (and the earlier #816-retarget pretick's own 30 -> 40 bump, see that step's own #1015 note) moves this step's own entry tick and lands the retired accept step (#1335) on a materially different rubble_disposal pool instance: deadlineTicks 31 (not #974's 46), acceptedAtTick 465, hauler's storedMassKg landing 9 ticks later at tick 474 (direct-traced, command mode, this retune). `tick 44` alone (landing tick 509) is 13 ticks past the instance's own deadlineAbs of 496 -- the delivery step right after finds the contract already expired. `tick 22` (landing tick 487) keeps 9 ticks of margin past the hauler's own load-in and 9 ticks of margin before the deadline, the same two-sided-margin philosophy #928/#974 used against their own instances. #1263 CI-fix: 22 -> 30 -- replacing the accept step's own upstream `tick 160` pad with a condition-based `wait_until rubbleDisposalOffered` (see that step's own #1263 note) collapses command mode's own entry to the accept step from tick 702 down to tick 543 -- the fixed `tick 160` used to pad command mode's trajectory 160 ticks past build-storage regardless of when the offer actually appeared (it appeared 1 tick in this run), and this step's own `tick 22` was never retuned against that padding being removed. Direct-traced (command mode, this fix): accepted contract is a fresh instance (id 26, quantityKg 120, deadlineTicks 58, acceptedAtTick 543, deadlineAbs 601) -- unrelated to any instance a previous round of this note measured, since accept now lands on a different tick entirely. storedMassKg is 0 through this step's own first 23 ticks and first lands its full 1050kg load at tick 567 (24 ticks after accept) -- `tick 22` alone (landing tick 565) is 2 ticks short. `tick 30` (landing tick 573) keeps 6 ticks of margin past the 567 landing point and 28 ticks of margin before the deadline (601), the same two-sided-margin philosophy every earlier round of this step used against its own instance. #1335: no rubble_disposal contract is accepted before this step any more, so the hauler's landing no longer races a contract deadline; the stored-mass landing tick is the only timing this step depends on.

expect.note: The old reported bug this beat guarded against (no UI control anywhere could trigger `vehicle haul`) no longer applies -- #552 retires the button and the whole manual flow, so there is nothing left to get stuck on. #1042 CI-fix: replaced the fixed `tick 200` + eight `tick 20` pad that stood here with the same `wait_until fillableOreSaleOffered` pattern #1048 already proved for this exact fragility in tutorial-steps-visual.json. #1042's evacuate-zone fix (a qualified employee now genuinely drives a driverless vehicle clear instead of the horn stranding it unconditionally) shifts every tick this file's own trajectory lands on downstream of Sound the Horn -- direct-traced (interaction mode, this fix): tickCount 680 after this step used to require `tick 200` alone to reach 771, and the old fixed pad of eight further `tick 20` calls (aimed at tick 832, where dirtite offer #47 was confirmed present under the pre-#1042 timing) instead rotated a fillable offer that was already on the board at 680 back out by 821 -- `fillableOreSaleOffered` read true at 680 and false again at 821, which is exactly the shape of failure #1048's own history describes: a fixed pad aimed at one pool instance breaks the moment anything upstream re-times the run into a different one. `fillableOreSaleOffered` (console-api.ts) waits on the real condition -- the pool holding an ore_sale asking no more of its ore than the site already has -- rather than a tick count guessed against one trajectory, so it holds regardless of how many ticks evacuate-zone or any future upstream change spends. Dropped the `material:dirtite` pin on the two steps below for the same reason: this pit's two blasts only ever produce dirtite in fillable quantity (every other offer this file's own history sees -- absurdium/rustite/craktonite/blingite -- is never actually held in storage), so a generic fillable match resolves to dirtite in practice without re-pinning the scenario to one pool composition an upstream retime can roll away from under it, same as #1048's own fix. #1091-followup: max_ticks 400 -> 4200 (timeoutMs 120000 -> 600000) -- #1090's dispatch-cost reordering changes the absolute tick this run's RNG stream rolls a fillable ore_sale offer on (same condition, different draw sequence; see the new_game step's own #1091-followup note on the matching cash bump this required). Direct-traced (command mode) the match now lands 3798 ticks into this wait (tickCount 4300), not within the old 400-tick budget. 4200 keeps ~400 ticks of margin above that measured landing point, the same margin-over-measured-landing philosophy every earlier retune of this exact step already used. #1131 CI-fix: max_ticks 4200 -> 60000 -- the #1091-followup retune above was measured in command mode only, and CI's shard 5/10 (interaction mode) stalled at max_ticks:4200 as a result. Direct-traced (interaction mode, real browser, this fix, same PR): this run's own RNG stream lands the match at tickCount 14100, 13634 ticks into this wait (it starts at tick 466) -- over 3x command mode's own 3798-tick landing, and well past the old 4200-tick budget. 60000 keeps ~46000 ticks of margin above that measured interaction-mode landing point; wall-clock cost of the extra ticks is cheap (this whole 53-step scenario, end to end, ran in well under 400s in this fix's own verification run) so the ceiling is set generously rather than tightly retuned, matching this file's own #1015/#1091 precedent of paying real margin over the measured landing rather than the minimum that clears it. Re-verified command mode at the same max_ticks: still lands at tickCount 4300 (3798 ticks in), unaffected -- raising the ceiling doesn't change where a mode's own RNG stream resolves, only how much headroom is left above it. See the new_game step's own #1131 CI-fix note for the matching cash bump this required (2,000,000 -> 50,000,000) to keep interaction mode's much longer wait solvent.

#959, the issue's own missing half, first beat: Accept clicked on an ore_sale offer this pit can actually fill -- rock its own blasts produced and its own haulers carried in. #1042 CI-fix: scoped to `[data-contract-type="ore_sale"][data-contract-fillable="true"]` rather than to `material:dirtite` -- which ore the board asks for is random per refresh (Contract.ts's generateContracts), so naming one pins this step to a pool composition that any upstream re-timing (like #1042's own evacuate-zone fix) re-rolls, same failure #1048 already fixed this same way in tutorial-steps-visual.json. `data-contract-fillable` is the card's own `stored >= quantityKg`, the same figure its "have" bar already colors green, and the DOM counterpart of the `fillableOreSaleOffered` the preceding step waits on. A `waitForSelector` ahead of the click gives the refresh cycle time to surface the right card rather than assuming it's there instantly. `commandOutcome: 'either'` is command-mode only: the two modes' tick trajectories diverge well upstream of here (this file's haul-debris step waits on the tutorial rail in interaction mode and on a fixed `tick 22` in command mode), so the same wait_until above lands command mode on a different offer pool, where the console can refuse this accept outright. The sell beat is proven by the click path, in interaction mode, which is the mode that models a player at all.

expect.note: The card is still 'sell-ore' after accepting: accepting an offer is not selling anything, and this step's own predecessor already proved a delivery of any kind no longer advances it. Only the completed ore sale in the next step does.

steps.description: #959, the issue's own missing half, second beat: Deliver clicked on the accepted contract, and with it the tutorial finally turns blasted ore into money. Nothing is typed into the amount field: ContractsPanel pre-fills it with `min(remaining, stored)` (`maxDeliverable`), so a plain click delivers exactly what storage can cover, which is the mechanic the 'sell-ore' card's own text teaches. #1042 CI-fix: click scoped to `[data-contract-type="ore_sale"]` alone (no `material:dirtite` pin, same reasoning as the accept step above) -- safe unscoped-by-material here because the accept step already narrowed the pool to exactly one active contract, the same way tutorial-steps-visual.json's own sibling step does it. `commandOutcome: 'either'` for the same command-mode trajectory reason as the accept step. Reaching 'set-policy' rather than 'sell-ore''s immediate successor is deliberate: 'finances' and 'needs' after it are auto-advance cards that move on by themselves after a fixed beat, so whichever is showing when this step's goal is evaluated would be a race -- 'set-policy' is the next card that waits for a click and therefore stays put once reached. Before #959 this beat did not exist at all: the tutorial hauled its muck pile to storage and then walked past it to the closing card.
